In the middle is a carbonate/transition-state part, containing a central carbon, a negatively charged oxygen, an oxygen connected to the acyl group, and an acetyl-like structure on the right; there are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Then reason the count: Count all non-hydrogen bonds by fragments. The left carbon/skeleton connections include R-C, C-S, C-C, C-R1, C-O, for a total of 5. In the sulfonyl/aryl part, C-S has already been counted, so continue to count S-O, S-O, S-Ar, and the 6 ring bonds of the aromatic ring, for a total of 9. For the central carbonate/transition-state part, count from after the left O, avoiding double-counting C-O, including O-central C, central C-methyl, central C-O−, central C-O(acyl side), O-acyl C, acyl C=O, acyl C-methyl, for a total of 7. The total number is 5 + 9 + 7 = 21.

method.method_draft: After describing the image, divide the structure into fragments and count non-H bonds in each. Count the left carbon/backbone attachments: R-C, C-S, C-C, C-R1, C-O = 5. Count the sulfonyl/aryl portion beyond the already-counted C-S bond: S-O, S-O, S-Ar plus six aryl ring bonds = 9. Count the central carbonate/transition-state portion from the left O onward, avoiding duplicate C-O: O-central C, central C-methyl, central C-O−, central C-O(acyl side), O-acyl C, acyl C=O, acyl C-methyl = 7. Sum 5 + 9 + 7 = 21.
